titleStmt.title: Memorandum From the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Allen) to President Reagan

div.head: Memorandum From the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Allen) to President Reagan
div.p: Al Haig recommends approval of the sale of F–16 aircraft for Venezuela (Tab A). Cap Weinberger agrees. Both argue that considerable policy damage with an important oil supplier would occur if we did not approve this sale. Disapproval would also mean that the Venezuelans would probably place an early order for either the French MIRAGE or Israeli KFIR, neither of which they like or want. (C)

Because this sale reverses a policy against first-line fighter sales to Latin America that goes back at least to the Nixon Administration, I asked the Secretaries to provide the memorandum for your review. (C)

We had hoped to induce the Latin nations to procure the lower performance, less expensive FX aircraft. However, the FX is unattractive to well-educated and professional airmen in Third World countries, and our Air Force has pursued a vigorous policy of selling sophisticated aircraft like the F–16 without prior interagency deliberation or adequate consideration of the real needs of recipient states in the Third World. You need to provide guidance, because other cases (Peru and Colombia, and others) will arise, with some nations wanting generous terms. Accordingly, I propose that you direct full consideration of this issue at the next NSC meeting. (U)
That we discuss this issue more fully at the next NSC prior to final approval. (U)
Tab A Memorandum from Secretary Haig

note.p: Confidential. Sent for action. A stamped notation at the top of the page reads: “The President has seen.” Copies were sent to Bush, Meese, and Baker.
There is no indication of Reagan’s approval or disapproval.
